en.title: Matrix Number That Is the Maximum of Its Row and the Minimum of Its Column
en.description:
Find an element that is greater than or equal to every element in its row (ties allowed) and less than or equal to every element in its column; if one exists, output its value, otherwise −1. All valid positions necessarily have the same value.

See the input protocol for this site's supplements to missing ranges and its recovery of typos in the source.
en.input: The input is N M, followed by N lines of M integers each. The original bounds 1≤N,M≤1000 and non-negative integers are kept; the original upper bound on elements is missing, and this site adds 0..10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 5; 1; -1. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Scan row by row, maintaining the minimum R of the row maxima and the minimum of each column; at the end, let C be the maximum of the column minima, and when R=C, output the common value.
